name: SymBase
author: Lázár Zoltán

provenance.from: AMOSTools/Extensions, out of aminet dev/amos/amostools.i386-aros.lha -- held in the corpus at sources/aminet-dev-amos/. Its author's README says the directory is "every AMOS extension I can find, cut down to just their token tables with the make_extensions.pl script", and names the ExoticA AMOS extensions wiki page as the list it works from.
provenance.redistribution: Not redistributed here as software: the file carries no code at all. It is a token table with the library stripped out from under it, kept for identification and detokenising.
provenance.note: ExoticA's AMOS extensions list places it at slot 21. Nothing here observes it in a program: the slot is the wiki's recommendation and no more.

notes: TABLE ONLY. This is an AMOSTools stub -- the hunk shell and the token table survive, both length fields read zero, there is no code, and every entry's two routine words are overwritten with `====`. So the NAMES, the parameter SPECS and, because an id is the byte offset of its entry, the IDS are the original library's; the behaviour is not here and the evidence tier cannot rise above `manual` until a real binary turns up. The reader is checked against CRAFT and MusiCRAFT, which are held both ways, and agrees with them entry for entry -- see parseAmosToolsTable in src/tokens/libtok.ts. 51 keywords, an xBase-style database: `db use` opens a .dbf, `db select`/`db goto`/`db skip` move, `db get$`/`db put$`/`db field` read and write, `db append`/`db delete`/`db recall`/`db pack`/`db zap` edit, `db locate`/`db found` search, `db order`/`db sort` index. Fifteen of them are RESERVED VARIABLES (spec `V0`) rather than functions -- `db sel`, `db recno`, `db reccount`, `db state` -- which is the distinction that has to be got right or they will not tokenise. FOUR RELEASES ARE IN THE ARCHIVE and they are FOUR DIFFERENT TABLES: 0.58 (35 keywords), 0.85 (46), 0.92 (54) and 0.94 (51). 0.58 against 0.94 keeps only 21 entries at the same id, so a program tokenised against one does not read under another; the other three are vendored here unregistered, and each needs its own entry if a program ever turns up that wants it. The corpus holds the SymBase 0.94 distribution (sources/aminet-dev-amos/files/SymBase/) with three AmigaGuides and an installer, but no .Lib -- `libinstall` puts one there, and what it puts is not in the archive.
